Package neqsim.process.engineering.pid

Class PidSafetyFunctionValidator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.engineering.pid.PidSafetyFunctionValidator
public final class PidSafetyFunctionValidator extends Object
Validates canonical P&ID safety-function settings against actual objects in an isolated process copy.

This is a binding and evidence-integrity check, not a safety lifecycle assessment. Physical independence, SIL, continuous-time constraint satisfaction, controlled standards compliance and engineering approval are not inferred. Call configuration validation again inside the scenario logic factory and compare its fingerprint before execution.

    • validateConfigured

      public static PidSafetyFunctionValidator.ConfiguredFunction validateConfigured(EngineeringProject project, PidDesignModel model, PidSimulationBindings bindings, ProcessSystem process, String functionTag, ClosedLoopSafetyFunction function, Map<String,SafetyFunctionChannel.FaultMode> faultOverrides)
      Validates explicit scenario fault overrides while retaining the healthy design settings.

      Required function attributes are simulationSifId, safetyFunctionRole, simulationVoting and simulationLogicDelaySeconds. Incoming instrument attributes are simulationTripUnit, simulationTripSetpoint, simulationTripDirection, and simulationResponseDelaySeconds. Actual ESD-valve targets require simulationStrokeSeconds and simulationFailSafePosition. Attributes govern configuration only when the caller reads them into the native factory and this check succeeds.

      Parameters:
      project - governed source project
      model - canonical proposal graph
      bindings - current explicit bindings
      process - configured isolated process copy
      functionTag - canonical function tag
      function - actual native closed-loop function
      faultOverrides - explicitly declared per-instrument scenario fault modes
      Returns:
      immutable configured-copy receipt
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if settings, connectivity or actual object identities disagree
